text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- New Chancellor Viktor Klima will change the whole Social Democrat government team. Women's Affairs Minister Helga Krammer will make way for Barbara Prammer. Interior Minister Caspar Einem will move into Rudolf Scholten's Science and Arts Ministry but may not take on the transport portfolio. State secretary for the civil service Karl Schloegl will become Interior Minister. Worker's Chamber head Lore Hostasch is to become the new Social Affairs Minister, possibly clearing the way for union chief Fritz Verzetnitsch and womens' Union chief Irmgard Schmidtleithner to take over her job.

- Conservative junior coalition partner the People's Party hopes the new government team will work together better. The party's leader Wolfgang Schuessel has reaffirmed his party's pledge to work with the Social Democrats.
- The Social Democrat grass-roots are against any form of coalition with Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party and would leave the party.

- Austria's state-owned postal service monopoly Post & Telekom Austria will raise its prices by ten percent in mid-1997. The higher postage fees are expected to bring one billion schillings per year. The post's regional bus system is to be partly financed by Austria's provinces.
- Steelmaker VA Stahl's profits nearly halfed to 1.6 billion schillings in 1996.
- New car registrations rose 10 percent to 307,671 in 1996.
- Air carrier Lauda-air's dividend wil remain unchanged after the company's net income fell to 50 million schillings in 1996 from 72.8 million the year before.
- An opinion poll by the industrial union shows the industry is sceptical about the development of Austria's economy and that the reduction of jobs will continue.
- Bank Austria and Creditanstalt will merge their activities in Eastern Europe.

- Economic research institute Wifo says the economy is better than the mood as 61.5 billion schillings were invested in 1996, 23.5 percent more than the previous year. Wifo expects a rise of 8.6 percent this year.
- 1,190 private households went bankrupt in 1996, mainly because of too much spending on holidays.
- As further privatisations are due within the provincial Hypo banks, the banks are holding talks about their strategic future.
- As illicit work is counted as part of GDP Austria's EU-fee will rise 709 million schillings to 31.2 billion.
